title: Macmillan Staff Say the Publisher Threw a Party for a Workplace AI Assistant That Was Later Killed
summary: Workers tell WIRED that NOA—or “No Ordinary Assistant”—was unhelpful. Bestselling authors also say AI is ruining their relationships with Big Five publishers.
llm_summary: Macmillan’s internal AI chatbot, dubbed NOA (“No Ordinary Assistant”), was celebrated with a launch party despite employees finding it largely useless and even disruptive. The tool was later discontinued, and several bestselling authors have now voiced concerns that similar AI systems are straining their relationships with the major publishing houses.
